Lessons.Title: Making a Model for Data
ExplanationParagraphs: Source-aligned goals: Compare and contrast different models for the same data. Use transformations to create a function that models data given a simple starting function.

Use observed vertices, intercepts and scaling to transform a parent graph. For a quadratic with vertex (1,3) and output5 at x2, g(x)=2(x-1)²+3 fits both; verify additional observations before trusting the model.

Source activity 11.1: What Function Could It Be?: What do you notice? What do you wonder? Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Source activity 11.2: Heating Up: Here is a graph of data showing the temperature of a bottle of water after it has been removed from the refrigerator. For the function types assigned by your teacher: Apply a sequence of transformations to your function so that it matches the data as well as possible. How well does your model fit the data? Make adjustments as needed. Explain the mathematical model, verify the relevant result and have a teacher inspect original diagrams or discussion evidence.

Practice Problem 1: A line \(\ell\) is defined by the equation \(f(x) = 2x - 3\). Line \(m\) is the same as line \(l\), but shifted 1 unit right. What is an equation for a function \(g\) that defines the line \(m\)? Line \(n\) is the same as line \(m\), but shifted 2 units up. What is an equation for a function \(h\) that defines the… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 2: The functions \(g\) and \(f\) are related by the equation \(g(x) = f(\text-x) + 3\). Which sequence of transformations will take the graph of \(f\) to the graph of \(g\)? Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
Practice Problem 3: The function \(f\) is linear. Can \(f\) be an odd function? Explain how you know Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 4: Technology required. The function \(f\) is given by \(f(x) = x^3 + 1\). Kiran says that \(f\) is odd because \((\text-x)^3 = \text-x^3\). Do you agree with Kiran? Explain your reasoning. Graph \(f\), and use the graph to decide whether or not \(f\) is an odd function. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 5: Here are graphs of three functions \(f\), \(g\), and \(h\) given by \(f(x) = (x-1)^2\), \(g(x) = 2(x-1)^2\) and \(h(x) = 3(x-1)^2\). Identify which function matches each graph. Explain how you know. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 6: Technology required. Describe how to transform the graph of \(f(x) = x^2\) into the graph of \(g(x) = 4(3x-1)^2 + 5\). Check your response by graphing \(f\) and \(g\). Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 7: Let \(p\) be the price of a T-shirt, in dollars. A company expects to sell \(f(p)\) T-shirts a day where \(f(p) = 50 - 4p\). Write a function \(r\) giving the total revenue received in a day. Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.

Practice Problem 8: A population of 80 single-celled organisms is tripling every hour. The population as a function of hours since it is measured, \(h\), can be represented by \(g(h) =80 \boldcdot 3^h\). Which equation represents the population 10 minutes after it is measured? \(g(10) =80 \boldcdot 3^{10}\) \(g(0.1) =80 \boldcdot… Preserve original numbers, constraints and representations in a student practice task.
